title: Two-literal contradictions are all or nothing in direction; three-place ones can be selective
claim: In every two-literal tiling world on a triangular torus, with or without coins shared between clauses, the classes along which a configuration contradicts are none, the multiples of one primitive class, or every class odd relative to the fitting twist: the doubly allowed tiling makes the parity of every closed implication walk the relative twist of its class. Hence a lone line is a pure line there, and the dual-pair failures of shared-coin worlds are failures of the line event itself. Three-place tiling worlds break the trichotomy: certified configurations contradict along some odd classes and not others, 12 of the 30 three-place placements do so on every torus computed, and a lone line can contradict along classes the lone event never checks; lines pure among eight classes still differ across dual pairs.
failure_conditions: A two-literal tiling world with a configuration that contradicts along some but not all odd classes and along more than one class.
A claimed three-place counterexample whose pattern is not certified both ways.
foundation_claim_scope: Twisted fair worlds on triangular tori with cylinder covers; exact statements and certified finite counterexamples. Lattices are declared; no space or physics is claimed.

validation.status: checked: prose proof; check.py (standard library) confirms Lemma 1 on all 24 two-literal tiling placements, Lemma 2 on all 32296 fundamental cycles of their clause graphs on 3 x 3, 3 x 4 and 4 x 4, Theorem 3 on 329 contradicting sampled configurations (every cylinder certified by its own two-literal solver), and Proposition 4 on three three-place configurations certified both ways by its own search; two controls rejected. Proposition 5 cites the frozen, independently checked experiment. No human or external review
